newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - April 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - April 21.

text.p: These were the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Political stability main reason for present economic boom, satys Deputy Finance Minister Gamini Lakshman Peiris.

President Chandrika Kumaratunga plants a spaling from the sacred Bo tree at India's Bodh Gaya temple near the Sri Maha Bodhi temple at Anuradhapura. The giant Sri Maha Bodhi tree is one of the world's oldest known trees.
Some 35 Sri Lankan fishermen and seven boats taken into custody by Indian coast guard near Dhanushkodi in South India
Government-registered medical officers to stage protest campaign on Monday against salary anomalies. A strike by government doctors last week left health services paralysed. ---
Water levels in hydro reservoirs down to about 18 percent of normal capacity as drought continues, threatening power cuts.
Current intermonsoon rains expected to develop into full-blown monsoon rains by next week, Meteorological Department says.
The gifting of a sacred Bo sapling from India to Sri Lanka symbolises goodwill among two countries, President Kumaratunga says at the planting of the sapling.
Sri Lanka records 75th AIDS patient at hospital in the south. The patient is a female foreign national, hospital sources say.
Government schools reopen on Monday for second term after Sinhalese and Tamil New Year holidays.
